# Prerequisite map

A valid study order (every lesson after its prerequisites):

1. L01-1 · How US and Florida real estate law is organized
2. L01-2 · The real estate business: sectors, specialties and organizations
3. L02-1 · Who needs a license: the three-part test
4. L02-2 · Exemptions from licensure
5. L02-3 · Qualifying and applying for a sales associate license
6. L03-1 · FREC and DBPR: structure and powers
7. L03-2 · License types, registration, group and multiple licenses
8. L03-3 · Keeping the license: post-license, renewal, CE and license status
9. L03-4 · Licensee duties to the DBPR: address, convictions, changing brokers
10. L04-1 · The three brokerage relationships and the transaction-broker presumption
11. L04-2 · The duty lists: 3, 7 and 9
12. L04-3 · Disclosure notices: timing, transitions, scope and exceptions
13. L04-4 · Material facts, designated sales associates, and ending relationships
14. L05-1 · Escrow accounts and the deposit clock
15. L05-2 · Conflicting demands and settlement procedures
16. L05-3 · Advertising rules
17. L05-4 · Offices, signs, compensation, kickbacks and rental lists
18. L06-1 · The complaint process
19. L06-2 · Penalties and the violation vocabulary
20. L06-3 · The Real Estate Recovery Fund
21. L07-1 · Fair housing
22. L07-2 · ADA, ECOA, HMDA and marketing rules (Do Not Call, CAN-SPAM, fax)
23. L07-3 · RESPA and TILA (TRID)
24. L07-4 · Florida Residential Landlord and Tenant Act
25. L08-1 · Freehold estates and the bundle of rights
26. L08-2 · Leasehold estates, lease types, assignment and sublease
27. L08-3 · Co-ownership: tenancy in common, joint tenancy, tenancy by the entireties
28. L08-4 · Florida homestead: creditor protection and transfer restrictions
29. L08-5 · Condominiums, cooperatives, timeshares, HOAs and CDDs
30. L09-1 · Acquiring and losing title
31. L09-2 · Deeds: types and requirements
32. L09-3 · Notice, recording and title evidence
33. L09-4 · Encumbrances: liens, easements, encroachments and restrictions
34. L09-5 · Fixtures and water rights
35. L10-1 · The three legal description systems
36. L14-1 · Math foundations: decimals, fractions, percentages and the percent triangle
37. L10-2 · Townships, sections and land measurement
38. L11-1 · Contract essentials, classifications and enforceability
39. L11-2 · Offers, counteroffers, options, equitable title and remedies
40. L11-3 · Listing agreements
41. L11-4 · Florida contract forms and required disclosures
42. L12-1 · The note, the mortgage and mortgage clauses
43. L12-2 · Assumption, default and foreclosure
44. L12-3 · Qualifying the borrower, usury and predatory lending
45. L13-1 · FHA, VA and conventional loans
46. L13-2 · Loan types by repayment and purpose
47. L13-3 · Primary and secondary markets, the Fed, and discount points
48. L14-2 · Area, perimeter and unit conversions
49. L14-3 · Commissions and net to seller
50. L14-4 · Profit, loss and appreciation
51. L14-5 · Interest, amortization, LTV and points
52. L14-6 · Florida transfer taxes: documentary stamps and intangible tax
53. L14-7 · Prorations
54. L14-8 · The closing statement: debits and credits
55. L15-1 · Real estate markets, supply and demand, and pricing tools
56. L16-1 · Value: characteristics and principles
57. L16-2 · Sales comparison approach
58. L16-3 · Cost approach and depreciation
59. L16-4 · Income approach, reconciliation and who may appraise
60. L17-1 · Investment analysis
61. L17-2 · Business opportunity brokerage
62. L18-1 · Florida property taxation: process and calendar
63. L18-2 · Exemptions, Save Our Homes and tax computation
64. L18-3 · Income taxes and real estate
65. L19-1 · Planning, zoning and land-use controls
66. L19-2 · Environmental hazards and regulation
